posts.title: new book out
posts.description: FOR READERS AGES 12 AND UP available in many formats, including audiobook on Amazon , Aubible , and kobo et GAlley REviewerI just finished reading Flickers of Light in a Nazi Darkness by Lisa Waller Rogers, and it’s a really moving read. I read a lot of historical books, but this one is special because it skips the boring battle maps and focuses entirely on the ordinary people in the Netherlands who risked everything. The book starts right when Germany invaded in May 1940 and goes through the scary Nazi raids of 1942. It shows how Dutch Jews had their rights slowly stripped away until they weren’t even safe in their own homes. The author tells the story through short biographies of regular folks who became secret heroes overnight. You get to read about everyday people who learned how to forge fake IDs, build secret rooms in safe houses, smuggle extra food rations, and sneak Jewish children away to safety. The author calls them “flickers of light” because their small acts of bravery bro

posts.title: Tien Fuh Wu, Chinese slavegirl
posts.description: Chapter 1 Our story begins a long way from here in China around the year 1890 in the coastal province of Zhejiang that bordered the East China Sea. Tien Fuh Wu, about age 6, was standing on a wharf with her father waiting to board a ferry to Ningbo, the large city south of the Yangtze River delta near where her grandmother lived. Tien and her father were going to pay her grandmother a short visit. Her mother was there to see them off. “Tien’s mother handed her a toothbrush and and a new washrag in a blue bag. Then she began to sob.” [i] Her mother’s sadness baffled Tien. Tien liked visiting her grandmother who was very prosperous and wore silk and satin gown and bought delicacies for Tien’s family to eat. It was her grandmother’s idea to have Tien’s feet bound as a sign of her refinement and make her more marriageable.
